(This is just a basic explanation so there may be some info gaps) Automatic means the gas produced by the fires bullet pushes the gun back and readies another round for firing. The hammer is also made ready when the gun is pushed back, allowing it to strike the following round. Holding down the trigger allows this to happen automatically hence “automatic”.  

So holding down the trigger means ratatatatatata

Semi automatic means the gun fires once per trigger pull. The gas pushes the gun back and that energy also caused the next round to be pulled up and ready to fire, but the trigger has to be released and pulled again. So part of the process is completed automatically but the gun can’t fire again until there is another pull of the trigger. Hence **semi**automatic. 

Pull the trigger once = bang. Then release the trigger and pull again = bang. 

You are correct that semi automatic guns don’t need to be reloaded between shots (like a musket) but the process is generally inherently slower than machine guns.

The problem is people took the definition of institutional racism (prejudice + power) and divorced it from any institution.

Racism is prejudice and discriminatory actions based on race. Anyone can be racist.

Institutional racism is when racism happens as part of an institution or organization. For example, a fire department has some Arab or Chinese firefighters maybe a black captain. But the lieutenants and the chief are all white. And that situation is intentionally achieved because of discrimination against the minority officers.

Institutional racism means that (if you are discriminated against) you can’t fight it within the system (in this case, internally in the fire department) because the whole institution is against you. (The people who have the power within the system are racist = institutional racism)

I’m glad I could help. And I’m happy to continue the discussion. One note: I can only speak for myself and I don’t claim to speak for anyone else nor any group (so my answers won’t be representative of all ‘2A people’). Also, my thoughts may seem dispassionate or blasé about egregious injustices but I want to discuss things as calmly and rationally as I can, without stirring up strong feelings and letting a conversion started in good faith to get off track. I’m not looking to score any ‘gotcha’ points on you. 

I think your question is a bit loaded. ‘Gassing and maiming’ sounds like any and all incidents of police dispersing a crowd are just violence for violence’s sake. I have seen protests happening all over the country that have been well organized, peaceful and exemplary of a robust exercise of first amendment rights. Characterizing all incidents of police uses of force at protests as  unwarranted is just as fallacious as characterizing all instances of rioting as stemming from protestors. 

I think that there have been clear instances of misconduct and abuse by police on peaceful demonstrators which should be documented, investigated and punished. However, I will also state that 

I believe that the push for increased accountability for police and the prosecution of bad police officers is laudable and needed. Any misconduct by an officer should be investigated and the officer should be held accountable. I’m sure that there are many instances of misconduct that go undocumented, uninvestigated and unpunished, which is an unfair reality. Ideally, there would only be good cops with no bad behavior. Since we don’t live in a perfect world we must do the best we can with what we’ve got. It is clear that the current state of affairs is not the best we can do but I feel that things are on the road to improvement. 

As for your first assertion, no I don’t believe the government is “trying to take over”. I think that things are tense for protestors and police alike. There are inexcusable actions by police like pepper-balling a woman and her mother in their car driving down the street (which should be handled like any misconduct incident) but there are other incidents that are not as clear cut. 

I’ve seen quite a few videos on a popular social media platform that are labeled as completely unprovoked abuse on defenseless protestors. Which it may or may not be. I feel like they miss two key contextual points. First, when police go out in riot gear, that’s not the appropriate setting for a dialogue about police reform with the rank and file officers. They are there for crowd control and to quell a riot swiftly. (Yes, I have seen videos with police agitating people and using the reaction as a cover to start wailing on people. Still, the protests need to be followed up by face to face meetings with a plan for changes)
Second, in the case of instances where police are closing off an area, or enforcing a curfew, a lawful order to disperse or the announcement of a curfew should be followed. If it isn’t, it shouldn’t be a surprise to face consequences for it. I’ve seen videos where a protestor is in the middle of the street facing a line of riot police and standing with their hands up not doing anything. Once the police announce that protestors need to disperse, then simply leave. If the city administration enact a curfew then go to them to change it, not the cop on the street.
